about: I am a PhD researcher in Geological Engineering based in Beijing, working at the intersection of geotechnical engineering, geohazard science and artificial intelligence.

My background combines geotechnical experiments and physical-mechanism studies with field and engineering experience in geological-hazard investigation, slope engineering, structural monitoring and urban infrastructure inspection.

My current research focuses on scientific AI for complex geotechnical and geohazard systems, particularly how sparse and heterogeneous observations can be used to understand system dynamics, forecast long-term evolution and failure, and support trustworthy engineering decisions.
I am especially interested in connecting real-world observations, physical understanding and modern machine learning.
contact: I am interested in discussions and potential collaborations around scientific AI, geotechnical systems, geohazards and long-term monitoring.
integration: Observations describe system states. Physical principles constrain plausible behavior. Domain knowledge connects material properties, environmental triggers and failure mechanisms. My developing research program asks how these sources of evidence can jointly support scientific learning of geosystem dynamics.
